publisher: وزارة الأوقاف والشؤون والمقدسات الإسلامية (Jordanian Ministry of Awqaf, Islamic Affairs and Holy Sites)
verdict: DEGENERATE: the publisher offers 16 regional labels and serves ONE table for all of them
provenance: The record's JO-AWQAF object notes 'governorate value 1 covers Amman, Balqa, Zarqa and Madaba', which reads as a per-governorate layer. Tested here: all 16 selector values were posted and each response confirmed its own label as selected while printing byte-identical times.

test.evidence: each POST echoes its own label in the selected option (e.g. 'العقبة') and prints 05:37:00 06:55:00 12:21:00 03:18:00 05:46:00 07:03:00, identical to region 1 on every row
test.whyItCannotBeReal: Aqaba and Irbid differ by 2-3 minutes in a genuine November table at 1 degree of latitude and 0.6 degrees of longitude apart; identical output on 60 cells is not a coincidence

notes: Values 10, 16, 17, 18 and 20-32 are absent from the selector; the numbering is a legacy database key, not a sequence.
The page serves a rolling 10-day window from tomorrow. Only November was observable, so the test is a November test; the degeneracy is strong enough there to stand.
Consequence for the resolver: Jordan must be modelled as ONE point with one recipe, never as a regional ladder. The 16 labels carry no time information.
